column2: Samson descends to Timnah, sees a foreigner's daughter there and is pleased; the repeated locality remains.
He reports to both parents and asks them, plurally, to obtain the woman as his wife; English get her for me carries the marriage request.
Both parents object, using my people in the selected speech; Samson replies to his father with a singular request and the eyes image.
column3: The singular my in a speech attributed to both parents remains a source feature, not corrected to our.

column2: The parents do not know the matter is from the Lord; he seeks recompense, while foreigners rule Israel.
column3: The subject of he was seeking is not named in Greek; lower-case he preserves the inherited openness rather than deciding between Samson and the Lord by capitalization.

column2: The three travel together, then Samson turns aside into the vineyard and encounters a roaring young lion; look represents the presentative particle.
The Spirit comes straight upon him; he tears the lion like a goat with an empty hand, and withholds the deed from both parents.
column3: Came straight upon represents kateuthyno as selected; its precise idiomatic force remains a lexical question, not a claim about physical trajectory.

column2: The descent and conversation verbs are plural, retained as they; the woman pleases Samson specifically.
His later return to take her includes a turn toward the carcass; bees and honey are in the lion's mouth, not silently relocated elsewhere.
Honey goes into his mouth, he eats while going and shares with his parents; he conceals its origin in the lion's body.
column3: Body for hexis is provisional in this context; the selected wording does not say he scooped honey into his hands.

column2: The father goes to the woman; Samson holds a seven-day drinking feast according to young men's practice, preserving both duration and feast type.
Their fear of Samson motivates assigning thirty companions; the text is not altered to say they merely saw him.
The proposed riddle has a seven-day deadline and two thirty-item rewards, linen garments and robes; neither category is collapsed.
The reverse condition imposes the same two thirty-item payments on failure, followed by their invitation to hear the riddle.

The eater/food and strong/sweet pairings retain parallel from-and-came clauses, followed by three days of inability to tell the riddle; authored display breaks make the couplet audible without changing wording.
The selected fourth day remains, with deception, threatened burning of wife and father's house, and the impoverishment question; no seventh-day replacement is made.
The wife's perfect-form accusations remain have hated and have not loved; Samson's behold and parent comparison precede the rhetorical question.
The seven days of weeping and seventh-day disclosure remain beside the prior fourth-day threat without chronological smoothing; she then tells her people's sons.
The city's paired honey/lion questions and Samson's paired heifer/riddle answer receive authored poetic line breaks; tamed is retained rather than importing ploughed.
The Spirit's coming precedes descent to Ashkelon, thirty struck men, their robes paid to the solvers, and Samson's anger and ascent to his father.
The wife lives with Samson's bridal attendant, also called his companion; the two designations remain.
Wheat harvest frames Samson's visit with a goat and proposed bedroom entry; the father prevents his entering to her.
The father's emphatic conviction that Samson hated her explains giving her to his companion; behold, the comparative younger sister and substitution proposal remain.
column3: I was certain compresses the emphatic saying and hatred constructions into the father's reported conviction; a closer repeated formulation remains possible.

column2: Samson speaks to the father but shifts to plural you in the threat of harm; this time retains the selected hapax expression.
column3: Ordinary English you does not display the Greek shift from singular recipient to plural threatened group; the evidence records it without supplying a new named audience.

column2: Three hundred foxes, tied tail pairs and one torch between each pair remain; no alternative animal identification is silently substituted.
The firing proceeds through sheaves, grain ears, harvested heaps, standing crop, vineyard and olive trees; the full extent of damage remains.
The explanatory report identifies Samson by marriage and the father's transfer of the wife; the foreigners burn the house, daughter and father, all three selected objects.
The conditional if-you-do-this and negative displeasure remain, followed by vengeance from each and every one; no until-I-am-satisfied conclusion is added.
The blow is upon the thigh, followed by dwelling beside the torrent in Etam's cave; no additional hip-and-thigh phrase is imported.
The foreigners ascend, camp against Judah and spread out at Lehi; the selected place form remains distinct from its translated counterpart later.
All Judah's men ask why they have come; the answer is to bind Samson and reciprocate his deed to them, retaining the retaliation formula.
Three thousand descend to Etam's rock opening; Samson answers as they did to us, retaining the selected plural us rather than the familiar singular me.
The announced capture and handover lead to an oath request against killing him themselves; both emphatic yourselves and the final lest clause remain.
Propose indeed bind for only bind, and but before the emphatic refusal to kill: the selected alla and de oppose binding/handing over to killing, without an exclusive only token.
column3: Indeed represents desmo desomen's emphatic binding construction; surely not kill preserves the separate emphatic death construction.

column2: Jawbone names the arrival point; the foreigners shout and run, the Spirit comes, and cords resemble flax fibre that smells fire before bonds loosen.
column3: The personified smell image remains even though a paraphrase such as touched by fire would be smoother.

column2: The donkey jawbone lies thrown on the road; Samson reaches, takes it and strikes one thousand men, with no fresh-bone description added.
The repeated with-a-donkey's-jawbone clauses and emphatic wiping out remain, followed by the thousand count; authored lineation preserves the two-part boast.
Finishing speech precedes throwing away the jawbone and naming the place Lifting of the Jawbone.
column3: Lifting for anairesis is provisional; taking away or removal may better convey the naming link and needs lexical review.

column2: Thou hast and Thy mark direct address to the Lord; great salvation by the servant's hand precedes thirst and the feared hand of the uncircumcised.
column3: The English treats the final futures as a distressed rhetorical question; the publisher punctuates a statement. A declarative And now I shall die remains an unresolved alternative.

column2: God opens the wound of the jawbone; water, drinking, returning spirit and refreshment precede the Invoked Spring name and continuing-time notice.
column3: The selected wound and jawbone construction is not replaced by a hollow in the ground at Lehi; spirit here concerns restored vitality without an inserted doctrinal explanation.

column2: Samson judges Israel twenty years in the foreigners' days; this closing notice is not suppressed because a later chapter repeats the period.
